Members, groups and the audit log
Add people, change roles and reset passwords.
Add a member, or import a roster from a CSV file.
The person gets a temporary password that is shown once. They choose their own password the first time they sign in.
%1$s gets a new temporary password and must choose a new one when signing in. The old password stops working.
%1$s is signed out and sets up two-step verification again at the next sign in. Use this when the phone was lost or replaced.
%1$s leaves this organization and cannot sign in anymore unless they belong to another organization. Their messages stay.
Their name, email and sign in details are erased and cannot be recovered. Their messages stay and show Former member. This only works for someone who belongs to no other organization.
Their name, email and sign in details are erased and cannot be recovered, and their messages are erased too. This only works for someone who belongs to no other organization.
Create groups and manage who is in them.
People who were removed, and finishing an erase.
People you remove from the organization are listed here.
Changes made by administrators are listed here.
%1$s changed the role of %2$s from %3$s to %4$s
%1$s changed the role of %2$s in a group from %3$s to %4$s
Create a group to message a team, class or department together.
Everyone else can read. Organization admins can always post.
Every member of the organization joins, now and when they are added.
%1$s and its group chat, including every message in it, will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
Everyone is already in this group

Add members to start the group conversation.
%1$s is removed from %2$s and from its group chat.
Add many people at once from a CSV file, such as an export from a spreadsheet. Each person gets a temporary password.
The file needs a header row with an email column. A name column and a role column (member, staff or admin) are optional. A missing role means member.
The temporary passwords are shown only once. Save them before you leave this screen.
The temporary passwords are not saved and cannot be shown again. You would have to reset each password.
The file has no rows to import.

A legal hold or an open report protects this group. It cannot be deleted until that ends.
An organization needs at least one administrator.
Something went wrong. Try again later.
On. Required for administrators and staff.

The reviewers your organization has chosen will see this message and the messages before it. The sender is not told.
It is also a crime. Tell the authorities as well.
Reviewers will not see your name. An organization admin can still find out who reported, and that is recorded.
A reviewer at your organization will look at it.

Unable to send the report. Check your connection and try again.

Reports sent to you to review.
Reports with this status will appear here.
This report is about a person, not a message.
This is the copy kept when the message was reported. It does not change if the message is edited or deleted.
The message was removed from the conversation. This copy is kept.
Keep the evidence and report it to the authorities. RA 11930 asks for it. Do not forward the files.
It is hidden from the conversation. The copy in this report is kept.
The reporter chose to stay anonymous. This is recorded in the audit log. Use it only when a report may be false or abusive.
The people you choose read and handle reports. Only administrators and staff can be chosen.
Nobody is chosen, so the organization administrators review reports. Choose people to change that.
%1$s showed the reporter of a report
%1$s changed how long messages are kept
Your organization may erase old messages after a set time.
Choose how long messages are kept.
Messages older than this are erased for good, together with their files. A legal hold or an open report protects the messages it covers until it ends.
The limit only takes effect when the retention job runs on your server. Your server administrator schedules it; see the compliance guide in the repository.

Create a file with the data your organization holds about %1$s, for an access request. It is recorded in the audit log. It holds the account, profile, groups, conversations and the messages they sent, not messages of other people, reports or the files themselves.
%1$s holds personal data. Share it only with the person who asked, or as the law requires. It is removed from this phone when you sign out.
Limit staff and student messages and set quiet hours.
No direct messages between staff and students
Staff and students can still talk in groups. Existing conversations between them become read only. Administrators are not held to this.
Nobody but administrators can send messages during these hours. Reading is not affected.
Times are in the time zone %1$s.
People in your organizations see Online next to your name while Mesgard is open. This applies to every organization you belong to.
Others see that you are online only if you choose. Students start hidden.
Protect data during a case or a legal order.
While a hold is active, what your organization keeps about the person or the group is not erased or deleted. Open reports protect the people involved without a hold.
Place a hold from a person or a group, or for the whole organization.
Nothing about %1$s will be erased while the hold is active.
%1$s and its group chat cannot be deleted while the hold is active.
Nobody in your organization can be erased and no group can be deleted while the hold is active.
It is listed under Legal holds in Administration, where you can release it.
A group that no longer exists
%1$s will no longer be protected by this hold.
Your messages and files are kept on your organization\'s server. Mesgard has no advertising, does not track you and does not sell your data.
Messages are not end-to-end encrypted. Your organization can keep and search them, for example when a report is made or when the law asks for it.
When a message is edited or deleted, the administrators of your organization can still see the earlier text.
When you report a message, the people your organization chose to review reports see that message and the ones before it.
This phone keeps an encrypted copy of your messages and files, and signing out removes it. A file waiting to be sent is encrypted once it is sent.
Questions about your data? Ask your organization\'s Data Protection Officer.
Your organization has not added a privacy notice yet. Ask your Data Protection Officer.
%1$s has a privacy notice. Please read it before you continue.
